faq.title:
Questions asked
before going into a pilot.
faq.description: We don't avoid tough questions. Here are honest answers to what enterprise teams ask most frequently.

items.q: How is Steloom different from a corporate knowledge base?
items.a: A knowledge base stores what you put into it. Steloom extracts structured knowledge directly from documents — automatically, source-linked, and in the context of your playbook.

items.q: Can we work with NDA-sensitive documents without sending them to external models?
items.a: Yes. Steloom supports a local-first processing mode with a PII-gateway before reaching out to external models.

items.q: What if the model makes a mistake — how will we see it?
items.a: Every system finding is tied to a specific source — clause, page, and document. Steloom was designed as an auditable system, not a black box.

items.q: How does the system handle non-standard contract structures?
items.a: Steloom does not rely on rigid document structure templates. Extraction works at the semantic level, not the formatting level.

items.q: Integration with our DMS / iManage / SharePoint — how long will it take?
items.a: Basic API integration takes 3 to 7 business days. Deeper bidirectional sync depends on your infrastructure. We discuss your specific stack during the demo.

items.q: Do we need a separate IT team for implementation?
items.a: No. Standard implementation is led by our team without drawing on your IT resources. Typical time from contract to first working review is 2 weeks.

items.q: How well does the system adapt to our playbook?
items.a: Playbook configuration is the core of the product, not an option. Steloom works with your review priorities, critical provisions, and risk-flagging logic.

finalCta.title:
Transform documents
into structure and knowledge
finalCta.description: Steloom gives your team structured, verifiable, and actionable knowledge from any set of documents — quickly, calmly, and without loss of control.

founder.name: Vladimir
founder.quote: Every legal conclusion must be grounded in documents, verifiable, and withstand professional scrutiny. That is why we built Steloom — a platform that does not replace legal thinking, but helps make decisions based on transparent, source-linked analysis.

knowledgeGrowth.title:
Growing
knowledge.
paragraphs: Steloom gathers thousands of disparate contract provisions into a single living structure — not for search, but to build your understanding through connections and context.

One document or a package of hundreds — the system works identically: it recognizes the type (SPA, SHA, NDA, employment agreement), builds the structure, and applies the risk set predefined by you for this specific deal or document.
Every finding is linked to its source — a specific clause in a specific document. No hallucinations, no detached generalizations.

hero.title: Generating Structured Results and Data
paragraphs: Steloom helps lawyers organize their work with documents (from one to hundreds of documents of various types) by systematizing them, checking for established risks/patterns, and generating structured results and/or data for further analysis.

The output is not a long text response, but a result suitable for further legal work: a DD grid by document types, a list of risks and comments with source references, and an understanding of what to look at first.

workflow.title: One verification pattern - from one document to hundreds - without losing result quality
paragraphs: For each document type (e.g., SPA, NDA, employment contract, corporate document, etc.), a specific analysis scenario and corresponding set of checks are applied.
One document or five hundred - each file goes through the same verification process, ensuring a uniform analysis standard regardless of project volume.
bullets: Automatic systematization of different document types
Custom analysis scenario or preset set of checks
DD grid based on key verification results
Uniform analysis standard regardless of project volume

structure.title: Analyzes the agreement and appendices considering their role in the document
paragraphs: Steloom automatically extracts the document structure, separates the main agreement from appendices, and maintains the connection between them.
The lawyer immediately sees where the relevant condition is located - in the main agreement or an appendix - and can evaluate it in the correct context.
bullets: Main agreement and appendices are analyzed separately
Each finding is linked to the relevant part of the document
Conditions in annexes and schedules are not lost during verification
Analysis considers document structure, not just continuous text

standards.title: Customizes document analysis to internal standards and team needs
paragraphs: Steloom verifies documents according to your organization's rules, not a universal template. This allows accounting for the team's internal practice, compliance policies, industry requirements, and approved corporate approaches to analysis.
The team can add checks for specific document types or set global rules applicable to the entire document package at once.

As legislation changes or practice evolves, rules can be updated without changing the overall workflow. As a result, documents are evaluated against uniform standards regardless of the executor or project volume.

findings.title: Structured results that can be verified
paragraphs: The analysis result is not a text response, but a set of findings, risks, and comments on documents. Each finding contains a link to the document, section, provision, or appendix on which the conclusion was based.
This allows quick navigation to the primary source, checking the context, and continuing work with the document.
Findings are grouped by document types and risk categories, forming a DD grid suitable for reports, internal review, and subsequent team verification.

methodology.title: Does not change the team's work methodology
methodology.leadIn: Steloom integrates into the existing process, it does not replace it.
paragraphs: The platform does not require restructuring the Due Diligence, internal review, or contract analysis process. Documents are loaded from familiar sources, and results are used in current reporting formats and the team's internal work.
The team can start with one scenario and gradually expand platform usage, preserving existing processes and familiar work formats.

cta.title: See how Steloom works with your documents
paragraphs: During the demonstration, we will show the full analysis path: document upload, type identification, application of checks, generation of findings, and a DD grid with source references.

If you have your own contracts or deal materials, they can be used as an example. This will allow you to evaluate the platform's performance in conditions as close to your tasks and internal processes as possible.

hero.title: Real Estate and Rights Analysis
paragraphs: Steloom identifies real estate objects in deal documents — addresses, cadastral numbers, and areas — and forms a project asset registry.
Each object is matched with external registry data (EGRN, DLD) for instant verification of rights and encumbrances.
hero.p1: In large-scale commercial real estate transactions and asset-heavy M&A deals, undetected title defects and unrecorded encumbrances can critically jeopardize deal value. Steloom automatically extracts addresses, cadastral IDs, land plot specs, and lease terms buried in unstructured Data Rooms.
hero.p2: Every identified property asset is instantly reconciled with primary state registry records (EGRN, DLD, Land Registries) to verify title continuity, identify active mortgages, and surface hidden liabilities before the deal closes.

items.title: Hidden Encumbrances
items.text: The risk of missing a mortgage, arrest, or easement recorded in appendices or historical documents.

items.title: Outdated Data
items.text: Discrepancies between the contract text and the current object status in the state registry.

items.title: Verification Complexity
items.text: The labor intensity of manually matching hundreds of cadastral numbers with current extracts.

i1.title: Hidden Encumbrances & Easements
i1.text: Pledges, third-party rights, and historical easements buried in annexes or historical title deeds routinely escape manual sampling, exposing the buyer to post-transaction litigation.

i2.title: Title & Registry Discrepancies
i2.text: Contractual descriptions frequently contradict current state registry data due to unrecorded zoning changes, illegal subdivisions, or outdated cadastral IDs.

i3.title: Manual Verification Bottlenecks
i3.text: Cross-referencing hundreds of contractual assets against fresh state registry extracts consumes hundreds of billable hours and delays deal closing.
